transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. I came in because... well, since my wife’s fall, I've just completely stopped functioning. I've always been the man with the lists and the plan, you know? Keeping everything organized. But now, I just sit at the kitchen table staring at her medication chart. I end up crying, or I'll just snap over absolutely nothing. And everything else is just piling up—the bills, my mentoring calls, even basic housework. It’s like I just can’t make myself do anything anymore.
How long ago did your wife's fall happen, and when did you start noticing these feelings and changes in your ability to function?

Well, her fall was only about two months ago. And... I didn't start feeling like this right away. I really started falling apart after the caregiving routine took over. Before that, I was completely fine. But once I had to manage all her daily care and that became my whole life, that's when I noticed I just couldn't function anymore.
Since this started, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even outside of the caregiving demands?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't really had the time or energy to even try doing the things I used to enjoy, with all the caregiving. But I don't think I've lost interest in them. I just... I can't get to them right now. If I had the chance, I'd still want to do my mentoring calls or read my history books, but I just can't seem to get past staring at the kitchen table.
Besides feeling sad and overwhelmed, have you also been feeling unusually anxious, worried, or on edge since your wife's fall?

I wouldn't say I feel anxious, no. It's not really worry or... or feeling on edge. I know what needs to be done for her care, the doctors laid all that out clearly. It's really just the sadness, and feeling completely paralyzed when I try to actually do anything. But no, I haven't noticed feeling panicked or unusually worried.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, like trouble falling asleep or waking up much earlier than usual, since your wife's fall?

No, my sleep has been pretty much the same. I mean, I'm exhausted by the end of the day with everything going on, so falling asleep really isn't an issue. I just go to bed and sleep through. I haven't noticed waking up unusually early or having any trouble like that. So, no, no real changes there.
